Leaching Loss of Nitrogen

Source: R/calc_N_leaching_loss.R
leaching_loss.Rd

DPI 2026 (Allegato 2; foglio C&D di Fert_Office v1.26): loss of readily available mineral nitrogen ("N pronto") from leaching.

Usage

leaching_loss(
  winter_rain = 160,
  start_spring_rain = 40,
  oxygen_availability = "Normal",
  id_rag = 3,
  b1 = 29.16,
  perennial = FALSE,
  autumn_loss = TRUE
)

Arguments

winter_rain

Winter rainfall (October 1 to January 31) in mm.

start_spring_rain

Rainfall in February in mm.

oxygen_availability

Oxygen availability level in the soil: one of ca.table$availability (e.g. "Normal", "Slow", "Fast").

id_rag

Soil texture group index (ID_Rag); retained for backward compatibility (not used in the formulas).

b1

Readily available nitrogen in the soil (kg N/ha).

perennial

Logical; TRUE for perennial crops in production (time coefficient 1), whose leachable pool is fixed at 30 kg N/ha.

autumn_loss

Logical; FALSE sets \(C_a\) to 0.

Value

A list containing:

C1

Autumn–winter leaching loss (kg N/ha).

C2

End-of-winter leaching loss (kg N/ha).

surplus_pluviometrico

Logical. TRUE when winter_rain + start_spring_rain >= 300 mm (DPI 2026 scheda a dose standard: surplus-pluviometric flag).

Details

Let \(N_p\) be the leachable N pronto: b1 for crops with a cycle shorter than one year, or a fixed 30 kg N/ha for perennial crops in production (perennial = TRUE, i.e. time coefficient 1).

C1 (\(C_a\), autumn–winter)

Depends on winter rainfall \(y\) (1 October – 31 January, winter_rain, mm): \(N_p \times \min(\max(y - 150, 0), 100)/100\), i.e. no loss up to 150 mm and the whole pool above 250 mm. It is 0 when autumn_loss = FALSE (first phase of a crop cycle, e.g. a second crop or pre-planting, as in Fert_Office).

C2 (\(C_b\), end of winter)

With \(s = y + f - 250\), where \(f\) is February rainfall (start_spring_rain): when \(s > 0\) the N pronto not yet lost (\(N_p - C_a\)) is lost, plus 1 kg N/ha for every 10 mm of \(s\) if \(y > 150\) mm.

oxygen_availability is validated against ca.table for consistency with other balance terms; the leaching formulas do not use it.

Examples

leaching_loss(winter_rain = 160, start_spring_rain = 40,
              oxygen_availability = "Normal", id_rag = 3, b1 = 29.16)
#> $C1
#> [1] 2.916
#> 
#> $C2
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $surplus_pluviometrico
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
leaching_loss(winter_rain = 300, start_spring_rain = 20, b1 = 0,
              perennial = TRUE)
#> $C1
#> [1] 30
#> 
#> $C2
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $surplus_pluviometrico
#> [1] TRUE
#>
